# AI Orchestration Update — 2025-03-30

## Summary

This update imports the modern AI orchestration infrastructure observed in [`andkov/caseload-forecast-demo`](https://github.com/andkov/caseload-forecast-demo) and [`GovAlta/quick-start-template`](https://github.com/GovAlta/quick-start-template) into the `archive-2025` branch of this repository.

All project-specific content has been preserved unchanged. The new `.github/` orchestration layer adds reusable agents, skills, prompts, templates, and orchestration guides for composing and publishing workflows — complementing the existing project-specific `ai/` persona and context system.

## How the Two Systems Relate

This repository now has two complementary layers of AI support:

### Layer 1: `ai/` — Project-Specific Persona & Context System

The `ai/` directory provides **project-specific subjectivity**:

- **`ai/personas/`** — Named AI personas (Grapher, etc.) with distinct analytical styles, epistemic commitments, and workflow preferences
- **`ai/core/`** — Dynamic context management that loads relevant project knowledge into AI conversations
- **`ai/project/`** — Project mission, methodology, and glossary (the "what we study and why")
- **`ai/memory/`** — Persistent memory tracks for human decisions and AI technical notes

This layer answers: *Who is this AI, what does it know about this project, and how does it approach analysis?*

### Layer 2: `.github/` — Reusable Orchestration Patterns

The new `.github/` directories provide **reusable workflow orchestration**:

- **`.github/agents/`** — VS Code agent definitions (invoked with `@agent-name`): Publishing Interviewer, Publishing Writer, Report Composer
- **`.github/copilot/`** — Skill files that teach Copilot when and how to invoke each workflow
- **`.github/instructions/`** — Scoped instruction files automatically applied to specific file types (`analysis/**`, `_frontend-*/**`)
- **`.github/prompts/`** — Bootstrap prompts for starting new workflows
- **`.github/templates/`** — Scaffolding templates for new analytical reports and publishing contracts
- **`.github/composing-orchestra-1.md`** — Design document for the Composing Orchestra (EDA/Report workflow)
- **`.github/publishing-orchestra-3.md`** — Design document for the Publishing Orchestra (website publishing workflow)
- **`.github/migration.md`** — Guide for importing these orchestration systems into other repositories

This layer answers: *How do we compose new analyses and publish the repository as a website?*

### How They Complement Each Other

```
ai/ (project identity)          .github/ (workflow machinery)
─────────────────────           ──────────────────────────────
Personas define WHO to be  →   Agents define HOW to work
Project context = WHAT        Orchestras define the PROCESS
Memory = accumulated WISDOM   Templates = reusable SCAFFOLDING
```

**In practice**:

- The `ai/` system shapes *how Copilot thinks* about this project — what terminology to use, what analytical stance to take, what project context to hold in mind
- The `.github/` system shapes *what Copilot does* — how to scaffold a new EDA, how to publish the repo as a website, what rules to follow when editing analysis files
- The two systems share the same files as inputs: `ai/project/mission.md`, `ai/project/glossary.md`, `ai/project/method.md` are referenced both by the persona system (for project context) and by the orchestration agents (as publishable content in the Project section of the website)

---

## Orchestration Workflows Now Available

### Composing Orchestra

Scaffold and develop new analytical reports (EDA or presentation Report):

```
@report-composer        ← Invoke the Report Composer agent
/composing-new          ← Bootstrap a new EDA or report
```

See `.github/composing-orchestra-1.md` for the full design.

### Publishing Orchestra

Publish the repository as a static Quarto website:

```
@publishing-interviewer  ← Start the publishing workflow (human-facing)
@publishing-writer       ← Execute assembly and rendering (non-conversational)
/publishing-new          ← Bootstrap a new frontend workspace
```

See `.github/publishing-orchestra-3.md` for the full design.
